levelMapping: ICT2 = junior (0-2 YOE); ICT3 ~ Google L4 / Amazon SDE II - Apple India (Bengaluru/Hyderabad) hires ICT3 at roughly 2-6 YOE, and even 5-7 YOE candidates are often offered ICT3; ICT4 = senior (~5-11 YOE; one 2024 candidate did two extra rounds to upgrade an ICT3 offer to ICT4). At ~3.3 YOE expect ICT3. Apple downlevels aggressively vs other FAANG, so confirm level and band with the recruiter early.

process.summary: Apple has no central hiring bar: each team runs its own loop, so round count (4-8+) and content vary widely; recruiters themselves sometimes do not know the order. Common India (Hyderabad/Bengaluru) backend shape in 2025-26: recruiter contact -> CoderPad/HackerRank OA (2 problems, 50-70 min, Java-only for Java/Spring roles) -> two back-to-back 60-min 'elimination' screens (R1: DSA + Java/Spring Boot/microservices fundamentals; R2: HLD+LLD, architecture, resume) -> a loop of ~3 more rounds (coding/concurrency, system design, EM/HM behavioral), sometimes extended with director/culture-fit rounds. Coding is practical: code must compile and run, you write and run your own test cases, and DSA is mixed with domain questions (Java internals, Kafka, Redis, SQL, OS/concurrency depending on team). Behavioral content ('Why Apple', conflict, ownership) appears in nearly every round rather than one dedicated round.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, role fit, 'Why Apple', comp expectations, notice period; recruiter explains (part of) the round plan.
rounds.probes: Ask for the full round plan, team and tech stack, and whether design rounds are HLD or LLD - recruiters often share, some even hint at questions.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.what: CoderPad (most common) or HackerRank, 2 coding problems; Java-only for IS&T Java roles; SDET/frontend variants add 15-20 MCQs. Easy-medium to medium.
rounds.probes: Reported OA problems: two-bag knapsack, grid path-following (collect letters along a unique path), walking-robot simulation, k-diff pairs, assign-cookies reskin, minimize-deviation reskin, LIS-style 'max cities' problem, string overlap factorization.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen / elimination round 1
rounds.what: 1-2 coding problems in a shared editor plus language/CS fundamentals; India IS&T version is DSA + Java/Spring Boot/microservices theory. Opens with intro + resume.
rounds.probes: Trapping Rain Water, parentheses, linked-list variations; Spring annotations, Comparator vs Comparable, CAP, rate limiting/circuit breakers, factory pattern; expect follow-ups that reuse your code.

rounds.name: Elimination round 2 (design + stack)
rounds.what: System design (BookMyShow, rate limiter, CI/CD) and/or LLD, plus deep tech-stack questions (HashMap internals, ConcurrentHashMap, BeanFactory vs ApplicationContext, caching).
rounds.probes: End-to-end flows (booking, search, onboarding, analytics), trade-offs, and theory depth; India loops treat this as eliminatory before the main loop.

rounds.name: Onsite coding rounds (x1-3)
rounds.what: LC medium-level problems with heavy emphasis on running code and self-written tests; often story-framed or practical (CSV parsing, iterators, concurrency).
rounds.probes: Thread-safety follow-ups (LRU, time-based KV store), complexity analysis, 'adapt your code' follow-ups, Java concurrency primitives, sometimes SQL.

rounds.name: System design round
rounds.what: One HLD prompt, or a deep-dive on your own project's architecture (common at Apple - some 'design rounds' are entirely your past project).
rounds.probes: Scalability, multi-region, observability, resiliency, data modeling; interviewers push back on choices and ask what you would redo.

rounds.name: LLD / domain round (team-dependent)
rounds.what: OOD with working code (parking lot, vending machine, pricing strategies, implement a Set), or domain deep-dive (Kafka/Flink, Linux internals for SRE, React for full-stack).
rounds.probes: Design patterns by name, SOLID, concurrency, extensibility; code review exercises (spot the pattern that improves given code).

rounds.name: Hiring manager round
rounds.what: Project deep-dive + behavioral (why change, conflicts with peer/manager, ambiguity) + light technical (Java 21 virtual threads, OAuth/JWT, REST).
rounds.probes: 'Why Apple', relocation flexibility, comfort with the team's specific work; STAR-format answers expected.

rounds.name: Behavioral / culture rounds
rounds.what: With senior leaders (senior manager, director for some loops); Apple values - deep expertise, drive for excellence, collaboration, invention, results.
rounds.probes: Mentoring, cross-org influence, disagree-and-commit stories; some US onsites are behavioral-heavy in every round.

rounds.name: AI-assisted coding round (new, some teams)
rounds.what: 2026 India Java loops report an 'AI assisted coding' round where you build with an AI tool; also recruiter-screen questions about how you use GenAI day-to-day.
rounds.probes: How you prompt, verify and test AI output; thin public info - ask the recruiter what tool and rubric they use.

process.indiaNotes: India hires are concentrated in Hyderabad (IS&T org - AiDP/GBI, Retail Engineering, Ads Delivery, data platforms; plus SDET) and Bengaluru (SWE, SRE/ACS, services teams). ICT3 is the default offer for 2-6 YOE (ICT4 from ~5-11 YOE with a strong case). India loops are stack-heavy: Java/Spring Boot/microservices questions carry as much weight as DSA, OAs are often Java-only, and the 2-elimination-rounds-then-loop structure is standard for IS&T. 2024-25 Hyderabad ICT3 offers: ~30-48L base + $92-168k RSU/4yr + 5-10% bonus + joining/relocation. IS&T has a vendor-heavy reputation (several candidates report interviewers converted from service companies) and mixed interview quality - rude recruiters, inattentive interviewers and ghosting appear in multiple reports. US/EU loops for the same band are more LC + behavioral and less tech-stack trivia; low-level teams (kernel, media) interview in C/C++ with OS internals.
process.timeline: Highly variable: fast loops finish in ~1 week; typical India IS&T loop is 4-10 weeks OA-to-decision; one 2026 Hyderabad offer took Oct (apply) -> Jan OA -> Mar screens -> Apr onsite -> offer 2 weeks later. Verbal-to-written offer takes 1-3+ weeks (multi-level approvals reportedly up to VP). Ghosting after rounds is common - silence is not always rejection.
tips: Ask the recruiter for the exact round plan, language constraints and HLD-vs-LLD split; Apple rounds are team-specific and recruiters often tell you (one was even told the exact question).
Practice in CoderPad with code that compiles and runs; write and run your own test cases - several rejections cite unrun/buggy code, and interviewers may stay silent instead of hinting.

For India IS&T/backend: revise Java internals (HashMap internals, equals/hashCode, string intern, immutability, CompletableFuture, executors, ReentrantLock/ConcurrentHashMap), Spring Boot annotations/beans, Kafka, Redis, SQL joins, CAP, circuit breakers.
Drill the thread-safety follow-up: LRU cache and time-based KV store were both asked with 'now make it thread-safe'.
Prepare one project to present in depth with metrics, trade-offs and 'what would you redo' - a design round may be entirely your project (bar-raiser-style HLD).
Prepare STAR stories (innovation, disagreement with peer/manager, reprioritization, feedback) and a crisp 'Why Apple' - it is asked repeatedly.
Expect pushback on correct answers; re-explain your reasoning calmly (two candidates report the same interviewer arguing LRU needs no DLL).
Follow up persistently with recruiters; timelines slip constantly and offers need many approvals.
process.notes: No bar-raiser; no fixed loop. OA platforms: CoderPad (dominant), HackerRank. Language: usually your choice, but Java-only for Java roles, C for kernel/low-level teams, JS/React live-coding for frontend/full-stack. LC-hard appears occasionally (a 2026 IS&T screen asked an LC-hard in 45 min; a 2026 US panel gave an LC-hard in 20 min). Some coding rounds are deliberately not LC-style: CSV parsing, iterators, debugging given code, concurrency. SDET loops = 1 OA + ~4 rounds (one DSA medium per round + automation frameworks + test design + HM). Full-stack loops add a React round (hooks, rendering 1M rows, component design). An LLD round exists but is team-dependent: IS&T 'elimination round 2' and loop rounds regularly include LLD/OOD with working code. Lunch is evaluative at in-person onsites; AI tools are banned in normal rounds (except the new AI-assisted round). India base pay is below Google/Microsoft parity but RSUs are large; negotiate with competing offers.

dsa.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
dsa.variant: Asked with a slight variation plus Java/Spring questions; follow-up: make it thread safe (candidate used ConcurrentHashMap). A Jan 2026 onsite asked the same API with TTL-expiry behavior under read-heavy load.
dsa.evidence: R1 of a 2026 Java/Spring loop (2026-09) and an onsite coding round in a Jan 2026 senior loop

dsa.title: Design Hit Counter / rate limiter class
dsa.variant: Recurring phone-screen staple: hit(ts)/getHits(ts) over last 300s. Follow-ups reported: do it in O(1) time (circular 300-slot array), avoid storing every hit (aggregate per second), and extend verbally into a distributed/sliding-window rate limiter (Redis).
dsa.evidence: Phone screens in 2026-08 (onsite loop PS1), 2025-09 (PS1), 2024-07 (O(1) follow-up); verbal sliding-window design in a 2026-10 SDE3 round; also flagged by an iCloud DB platform onsite report

dsa.title: Valid Parentheses
dsa.variant: Appears as the warm-up coding question alongside backend-fundamentals grilling (Kafka, SQL joins, Redis internals).
dsa.evidence: R1 of a 2026-04 Java/Spring loop; 2022 HackerRank OA; a Nov 2025 US onsite coding question

dsa.title: Paths in Matrix Whose Sum Is Divisible by K
dsa.variant: Sole question of a 60-min loop coding round (candidate linked the exact problem).
dsa.evidence: Loop round 1, Hyderabad Ads Delivery team (2025-11)

dsa.title: Minimum Runes to Add to Cast Spell
dsa.variant: LC Hard asked in a 45-min IS&T DSA screen; candidate solved in O(n+m) in 40 min and was still pushed for 'a more optimized solution' in the last 5 minutes.
dsa.evidence: IS&T coding screen (2026-06, reject)

dsa.title: Random Pick with Weight (country generator with population bias)
dsa.variant: Framed as: return a random country where probability is proportional to population. Expected solution: prefix-sum of weights + binary search; using random.choices() directly is not accepted. Related: an ICT3 full-stack onsite asked to sample n items while preserving the original distribution.
dsa.evidence: Apple round 1 (2026-07); distribution-preserving sampling in a 2025-03 ICT3 onsite

dsa.title: Product of Array Except Self
dsa.variant: Asked as 'print product of all length n-1 subsets' with explicit zero-count cases (no zero / one zero / many zeros); follow-up: no-division prefix/suffix approach.
dsa.evidence: Apple round 1 (2026-07)

dsa.title: Subset sum (exists + enumerate)
dsa.variant: Asked as: is a subset with a given sum possible (1D DP, O(n*target)); follow-up: print all subsets with that sum (backtracking, O(2^n)).
dsa.evidence: Apple round 1 (2026-07)

dsa.title: Phone directory (bidirectional name<->number lookup)
dsa.statement: Build a phone-directory class supporting add(name, phone), get_name(phone), get_phone(name) and removal by either key, keeping both directions consistent when an existing name or number is reassigned. Expected: two hash maps with careful cleanup of stale mappings (a trie is acceptable but overkill).
dsa.evidence: Apple round 1 (2026-07); also the DSA round of a 2022 ICT3 India loop

dsa.title: Sentence combinations from word lists ('pretty odd statements')
dsa.statement: Given a list of word groups like {The,A} {dog,cat} {runs,walks} {quickly,slowly} {.,!}, print every sentence formed by picking one word per group, in order (cartesian product via recursion/backtracking). Modular, OOP-style code was expected, not just a nested loop.
dsa.variant: A Jan 2024 Hyderabad phone screen gave buggy code for the same 'generate all sentences from word lists' problem and asked the candidate to debug it.
dsa.evidence: SSE round 1 (2026-02); debug variant in Hyderabad phone screen (2024-01)

dsa.title: SQL: joins and aggregation
dsa.statement: Write SQL against 2 given tables: reported variants include a join producing a set-difference (MINUS-style) result, a plain two-table join, and 'top earners per department' (group-wise max). Asked inside coding rounds, not a separate round.
dsa.evidence: ICT4 Hyd R1 (2026-01), SSE R2 (2026-02), 2024 ICT3 loop, DE loops

dsa.title: Find Peak Element
dsa.evidence: ICT4 Hyderabad backend R1 (2026-01); a 2026-04 kernel round also asked a medium binary-search problem in C

dsa.title: Count ways to split n items into k boxes
dsa.statement: Given n identical-value items and k boxes, count the ways to partition n into k distinct positive parts (no duplicate part sizes); e.g. n=3, k=2 -> 2 ([3],[1+2]). Solved with DP (integer partition into k distinct parts).
dsa.evidence: ICT4 Hyderabad backend R1 (2026-01)

dsa.title: Bowling game scorer
dsa.statement: Compute the final score of a bowling game from a sequence of rolls, handling strikes, spares, misses and the 10th-frame special cases. Implementation-heavy: the candidate (a self-described fast coder) needed the full hour, and the interviewer ran many test cases.
dsa.evidence: ICT4 Hyderabad backend R2 (2026-01)

dsa.title: Socket message reader interface
dsa.statement: Implement an interface that reads complete messages from a network socket where each underlying read returns a variable number of bytes; buffer partial reads across calls (closest LC analogue: Read4 II). Clean, testable code mattered - the reject feedback cited weak low-level protocol understanding and no test cases.
dsa.evidence: Phone screen 2 (2025-09, reject)

dsa.title: Top-K closest pairs in a sorted array
dsa.statement: Given a sorted array like [1,2,4,7,11,16], define a pair's distance as |a-b| for adjacent-or-any pairs and return the K pairs with smallest distances (K=2 -> [(1,2),(2,4)]). Heap over adjacent gaps / k-smallest-pairs pattern.
dsa.evidence: Onsite coding round 4 (2026-08)

dsa.title: Debug a KV-store scan iterator (Java)
dsa.statement: Read existing Java code implementing a key-value store's range-scan iterator, find the bug and fix it. Checks: scan start/end boundaries, skipped or duplicated entries, and iterator behavior after exhaustion.
dsa.evidence: Onsite coding-debug round (2026-08)

dsa.title: String overlap factorization (merge two strings on max overlap)
dsa.statement: Concatenate two ASCII strings so that the longest substring shared between the end of one and the start of the other is written once; choose the concatenation order giving the best factorization, preferring str1+str2 on ties (e.g. '1234yyabc' + 'abcxxxx1234' -> 'abcxxxx1234yyabc').
dsa.evidence: SDET IS&T OA (2026-09)

dsa.title: Endianness check + kernel deadlock debug (C)
dsa.statement: 45-min CoderPad round, all in C: (1) write code to detect machine endianness; (2) debug a kernel module containing a deadlock plus other optimization issues; (3) a medium binary-search problem. Explaining your thought process out loud mattered as much as solving.
dsa.evidence: Kernel/Core-OS CoderPad round (2026-04)

dsa.title: Go-board capture count (board simulation)
dsa.statement: Given a Go-like board of black/white/empty cells and the coordinates where a black stone will be placed, return how many white stones get captured (groups with no remaining liberties) - flood-fill/BFS over white groups. Similar to a known Google 'Go game' question.
dsa.variant: A 2024-10 phone screen asked a related state-space search: a 4x4 board of X/Y/empty stones, min moves (sliding a stone to any empty cell) to get 4-in-a-row, or -1.
dsa.evidence: ICT5 phone screen (2025-10); stones variant in a 2024-10 SWE phone screen

dsa.title: Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree
dsa.variant: Given a sorted linked list, build a height-balanced BST; discussed both the convert-to-array and in-place middle-node approaches.
dsa.evidence: Phone screen (2025-10)

dsa.title: Merge Intervals
dsa.variant: Asked alongside resume-driven HLD discussion in a single technical round.
dsa.evidence: Hyderabad technical round (2025-11); also top-5 in Apple's LC-tagged bank

dsa.title: Number of Islands
dsa.variant: Asked with complexity follow-ups in a 2-question DSA round.
dsa.evidence: India DSA round (2025-11)

dsa.title: LRU Cache (thread-safe)
dsa.variant: Full working code with test cases, then: make it thread safe (ReentrantReadWriteLock + ConcurrentHashMap), complexity, plus Java trivia (string intern, equals/hashCode). Two candidates report the same interviewer disputing the need for a doubly linked list - defend your design.
dsa.evidence: IS&T Hyd loop R5 (2025-06, plus an identical report in comments); Seattle phone screen (2025-04); comment prep-advice for Core Services screens (2026-09)

dsa.title: Trapping Rain Water
dsa.variant: 30 minutes of a 60-min round, followed by Java/Spring theory; also appeared in the 2022 OA and as a variation in an intern round.
dsa.evidence: IS&T Hyd elimination R1 (2025-05); 2022 HackerRank OA; intern round (2024)

dsa.title: Top K Frequent Elements
dsa.variant: Asked twice in India loops as a quick second problem after design discussion; expect to compare heap vs bucket-sort approaches.
dsa.evidence: IS&T Hyd loop R4 (2025-06); Java backend R1 (2025-02)
